title: The maximal difference theorem for s-numbers
abstract: A bound between all s-numbers (in the sense of Pietsch). The approximation  numbers a_n are the largest s-number sequence and the Hilbert numbers h_n  the smallest, so that h_n(S) <= s_n(S) <= a_n(S) holds for every s-number  sequence (s_n) and every bounded linear operator S between Banach spaces.  The formalized result gives a bound in the reverse direction:  a_n(S) <= ((n+1)^(n+1)/n^n) * h_n(S) <= e * (n+1) * h_n(S), for every bounded linear operator between normed spaces over the reals or the complex numbers. Hence, the same factor bounds the gap between any two s-number  sequences. The linear growth in n is order-optimal.  This is the main result of arXiv:2608.05024 and solves a problem of  Mityagin, Henkin (1963) and Carl, Pietsch (1978), up to a constant.
